speaker: Doctor
text: I have noted your symptoms of chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort. To begin our investigation, how many bowel movements do you have per day, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the detailed description; the relief of pain after defecation and mucus are significant clues. Did you experience any fever or unintended weight loss during these four months? Additionally, did anyone else in your camping party develop similar symptoms?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), C-Reactive Protein (CRP)

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any recent weight change, fever, nausea, or vomiting. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That diagnosis seems unlikely given your specific symptoms of rectal urgency, mucus, and incomplete evacuation; could you clarify how you are currently managing your condition, and do you have access to any stool studies or imaging from your previous visit? Please confirm if you have any history of inflammatory bowel disease or recent travel beyond that camping trip.

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ulcerative Colitis (likely mild-to-moderate left-sided). The history of chronic diarrhea, mucus, urgency, relief with defecation, and the relief of pain after bowel movement are classic for inflammatory bowel disease, specifically ulcerative colitis. The previous diagnosis of migraine is incorrect, and further testing is needed to confirm inflammation and rule out infection given the camping history. I recommend a Colonoscopy with biopsy immediately.
